key_insight: For high-wavenumber Helmholtz problems in 2D and 3D, the paper proves optimal inf-sup scaling μ ≍ k⁻¹ for both full-space and truncated uniaxial perfectly matched layers under specified absorption-profile conditions.
engineering_relevance: These results support reliable finite element simulation of high-frequency wave propagation using absorbing layers to truncate unbounded domains.
method: Establish wavenumber-explicit stability for full-space UPML with admissible piecewise-power absorption profiles.
Transfer the optimal inf-sup estimate to truncated UPML domains.
Derive preasymptotic error estimates for linear continuous interior penalty FEM.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical predictions and demonstrate CIP-FEM effectiveness at high wavenumbers, though the abstract gives no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The stability guarantees require specific absorption-profile regularity and derivative bounds near the onset of absorption; they do not cover arbitrary UPML profiles.
paper_title: Optimal stability estimates and preasymptotic error analysis of the CIP-FEM for the Helmholtz equation with uniaxial perfectly matched layers
